simple.meaning: כָּסַם (kâçam) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to shear.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 2 times in Ezekiel, beginning at Ezekiel 44:20. Its meaning becomes clearer as the uses are compared.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to כָּסַם (H3697) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: כָּסַם (kâçam) / H3697 is traced through Ezekiel 44:20 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.full: H3697. kasam [ כָּסַם ] verb shear, clip (Assyrian kasâmu, cut in pieces, according to Dl HWB 344 ); — only Qal Imperfect and Infinitive absolute אֶתרָֿאשֵׁיהֶם יִכְסְמוּ כָּסוֺם Ezek 44:20 they shall by all means clip their heads (opposed to יְגַלֵּ֔חוּ shave and יְשַׁלֵּ֑חוּ , i.e. let grow freely ).
